"Fallin'" is a song recorded by American pop singer Connie Francis in 1958. Here are the key details about this recording:

## Background and Recording
- Written by Neil Sedaka and Howard Greenfield, who were a prolific songwriting partnership
- Recorded when Francis was establishing herself as a major pop star
- Part of her string of recordings for MGM Records

## Chart Performance
- Released as a single in late 1958
- Reached #30 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart
- This was one of several charting singles for Francis during her peak years of 1958-1964

## Musical Context
- The song showcases Francis's distinctive vocal style with its emotional delivery
- Features the pop production style typical of the late 1950s
- Came during the same era as her bigger hits like "Who's Sorry Now" and "Stupid Cupid" (both 1958)

## Significance
- While not one of her biggest hits, "Fallin'" contributed to Francis's remarkable run of chart success
- Demonstrates the successful collaboration between Francis and the Sedaka-Greenfield songwriting team
- Neil Sedaka would later become a successful recording artist himself

The song represents the kind of quality pop material that helped establish Connie Francis as one of the most successful female vocalists of the pre-Beatles era.
